name: Can I live on-site during a luxury remodel?

mainEntity.name: Is it realistic to stay in the home during a high-end remodel or full rebuild?
mainEntity.text: Is it realistic to stay in the home during a high-end remodel or full rebuild?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether a homeowner can stay in the house depends on the scale of the project. A small renovation may allow partial occupancy, but a major luxury remodel or full rebuild usually creates too much disruption for normal living. Safety, dust, noise, utility shutdowns, and access restrictions are the main issues. In high-end projects, privacy and daily routine matter too, and living on-site can make both design and construction coordination harder. Homeowners should ask the builder to outline what areas will be unusable, how separation will be maintained, and what the realistic impact on the household will be. If the project includes structural work, major MEP changes, or phased demolition, off-site living is often the better choice. The right decision depends on the scope, tolerance for disruption, and duration of the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Living on-site during a major luxury remodel is sometimes possible, but it depends on the scope, safety, dust control, utilities, and privacy. Full rebuilds usually require the home to be vacant. Large remodels with structural work or multiple trade phases are often disruptive even when occupancy is technically possible.
